verses.1: And one day, while he was teaching the people in the temple, the high priests and the officials, along with the elders, offered sacrifices to him.
verses.2: And they said to him, “In what authority do you do these things? Who is the one who gives you this authority?”
verses.3: Then he replied to them, “I would like to speak with you. Please tell me what you have to say.”
verses.4: Was John’s baptism from heaven or from humans?
verses.5: And those who were gathered together said to each other, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ they will say, ‘Why don’t you believe it?’”
verses.6: But if we say that, “Out of all people, the crowd will surely reject us.” This is because they are convinced that John is indeed a prophet.
verses.7: And they said they didn’t know where it came from.
verses.8: And Jesus said to them, “I also tell you that in this same way, you will do these things.”
verses.9: He began to speak to the people about this parable. A man planted vines, and from them were produced grapes. These grapes were then sold by farmers, and they brought in good profits over time.
verses.10: And at the right time, a slave was sent to the farmers, asking them to give him some of the grapefruit as payment. But the farmers sent him away, saying that there was nothing to give him.
verses.11: And they also sent another slave as a gift. But when those slaves were tested and found to be unworthy, they were sent away empty-handed.
verses.12: And a third group was also sent out to attack them. But those who were injured in this attack also were killed.
verses.13: But the master of the vineyard said, “What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will be convinced by him.”
verses.14: Seeing him, the farmers began to argue with each other. They said, “This man is the heir! Let’s kill him, so that our inheritance can be ours.”
verses.15: And when they brought him out of the vineyard, they burned him. What will then the Lord of the vineyard do to them?
verses.16: He will also destroy these farmers, and give the wine to others instead. But when they heard this, they said, “That cannot be done.”
verses.17: And he looked at them and said, “What is this thing that’s written here? A stone that was rejected by those who built houses, has become the head of a column.”
verses.18: Everyone who falls onto that stone will be injured. And whoever falls on it will also be harmed.
verses.19: And the priests and high priests asked to be blessed by him in that same hour. They were afraid of the people, for they knew that he had said this as a joke.
verses.20: And upon seeing this, they sent out their own lawyers, claiming that they were the rightful authorities to handle this matter. This was done so that they could get him to submit to the laws and authority of the ruler.
verses.21: And they asked him, saying, “Teacher, we know that you speak truth and teach rightly. You do not take revenge, but rather truly follow the path of God.”
verses.22: Shall we give Kaisar more time, or not?
verses.23: After understanding their plan, he said to them:
verses.24: Please show me a coin. Who has an image and inscription on it? They replied, “The Emperor.”
verses.25: And he said to them, “Therefore, give back to the Emperor what belongs to the Emperor, and to God, what belongs to God.”
verses.26: And they were unable to prevail in their efforts to change the name against the will of the people. In amazement at his response, they turned away from him.
verses.27: Some of the Sadducees came forward. They understood that this wasn’t a revival at all. So they asked him questions.
verses.28: They said, “Teacher, Moses wrote that if a brother dies without having a wife, and he is still alive, then his brother may take his wife and restore his brother’s lineage.”
verses.29: So, there were seven brothers. The first one, after taking a wife, died childless.
verses.31: And the third one also took her. Similarly, the seven others didn’t even have any children, and they all died.
verses.33: So, what kind of woman becomes one in this transformation? After all, she is considered a woman by those seven people.
verses.34: And Jesus said to them: “The children of this world marry and are given in marriage.
verses.35: But those who are grateful for the coming of that season, and for the resurrection from the dead, neither marry nor are they married.
verses.36: For they still cannot die; they are sons of God, sons of the Resurrection.
verses.37: For the dead are being raised, and Moses warned about this, as did the chief priests of God: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.38: But the god is not one who dies; he continues to live. For all people live under his rule.
verses.39: Some of the officials replied, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”
verses.40: For there is no longer any reason to try to harm him.
verses.41: He said to them, “How can they say that Christ is the son of David?”
verses.42: For David said this in his Psalms. He said, “Lord, my Lord!” He sat to my right.
verses.43: Until I have defeated your enemies under the weight of your feet.
verses.44: So, he is called “Lord”. And what is his son’s name?
verses.45: But Akoountos said to all the people, to his disciples:
verses.46: Be careful of those officials who walk around in their uniforms, who kiss medals during meetings, and who take the lead roles at banquets.
verses.47: Those who destroy the homes of others and pray for their punishment in advance will suffer even greater punishment.
